newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario Hydro nuke shutdown planned over next year.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro nuke shutdown planned over next year.

text.p: Ontario Hydro, North America's largest power utility, said on Wednesday a temporary shutdown of seven nuclear units will be implemented over the next year.
"That is as detailed a timetable as I have heard. Over the next year the seven units will be laid up," Ontario Hydro spokesman Alan Manchee said in a telephone interview.
The utility earlier announced plans to lay up four units at the Pickering A station and three units at the Bruce A station. A fourth unit at Bruce A has been laid up since 1995.
The Pickering units have a generating capacity of 500 megawatts each, while the Bruce units have a capacity of around 800 megawatts each.
"In total round terms, 4000 to 4500 megawatts of capacity will be affected," Manchee said.
A heavy water plant at Bruce will be permanently shut down, Ontario Hydro said.
The electricity generated by the affected nuclear units will be replaced by operating existing fossil fuel plants at Nanticoke and Lambton at higher levels.
Naticoke's eight units have a total generating capacity of 4000 megawatts, while Lambton's four units have a total capacity of 2000 megawatts.
Nanticoke and Lambton are so-called peaking stations used primarily during peak demand periods. "The plan is to run them more than they are now, but just how much I don't know," Manchee said.

Ontario Hydro will also bring two mothballed, oil-fired units at the Lennox station back into service. Each unit has a generating capacity of 500 megawatts. Lennox's four units have a total generating capacity of 2000 megawatts.
Aside from the shutdowns, Ontario Hydro is planning an extensive upgrade of the Pickering B station, the Bruce B station, and Darlington station.
The cost of the entire overhaul is estimated at between C$5.0 billion and C$8.0 billion over the next five years, starting this year.
Ontario Hydro chairman Bill Farlinger said the overhaul will not affect rates. He added the utility will meet the electricity supply needs of its customers.
